title: WHO: malnutrition includes undernutrition, micronutrient imbalance, and overweight
summary: WHO's malnutrition fact sheet, dated 1 March 2024, defines three groups and says nearly half of deaths under age 5 are linked to undernutrition.
body: WHO's malnutrition fact sheet, dated 1 March 2024, says malnutrition refers to deficiencies, excesses, or imbalances in a person's intake of energy and nutrients. It names three broad groups: undernutrition, including wasting, stunting, and underweight; micronutrient-related malnutrition, a lack or an excess of vitamins and minerals; and overweight, obesity, and diet-related noncommunicable diseases such as heart disease, stroke, diabetes, and some cancers. It says nearly half of deaths among children under 5 are linked to undernutrition, and that these mostly occur in low- and middle-income countries. The "nearly half" is the sheet's statement about deaths. It is not a count of named children.
